text:
ops_incident_bot: ALERT: p99 latency > 3.0s on prod-usw2 continuous-batching path for model redwood-llama-quant. Rolling window: 10m. Paging eng-oncall. <https://dash.company/alerts/1777|view alert> :rotating_light:

alex_oncall: I'm oncall, ack. Starting triage — grabbing traces and recent deploys.

sam_sre: I see p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 900ms, p99 ~600ms -> 3.2s in the last 8m. Streaming requests also showing stalls (clients see long silence).

jia_runtime: Pattern looks like big batches with lots of padding. Mixed sequence-length traffic spiking batch sizes and causing KV cache eviction pressure. Could be padding amplification.

nina_support: Any customer-facing impact? Support queue shows two escalations in last 12m from customers on Dedicated clusters in usw2.

alex_oncall: Quick customer triage: affected tenants: corp-alpha (dedicated-usw2), edu-scope (hosted-usw2, high streaming load). Not widespread yet but high SEV for those tenants.

sam_sre: Dumping recent scheduler state and batch histograms:
```
# last 5m batch size distribution (prod-usw2):
median=8, mean=42, p95=128, p99=256
# seq-len mix: short(<64)=68%, long(>512)=12%, remainder mid
```
jia_runtime: That explains it — continuous-batching is coalescing many requests into large batches because of a small number of very long requests. Short requests wait and then get amortized into huge padded tensors.

alex_oncall: Mitigation options: 1) temporarily cap batch_size or drop into low-batching mode; 2) enable short-request prioritization in scheduler (favor_short_seq); 3) force fallback to smaller model variant for affected tenants; 4) disable streaming batching to avoid stalls.

sam_sre: I'm going to try a live mitigation: set `batch_size_dynamic_cap=64` for the slot pool handling redwood-llama-quant. If that fails, we'll shift to `batching_mode=latency-first` which disables large coalescing for streaming.

deploy-bot: @sam_sre config change submitted: `PATCH /config/pools/prod-usw2/slotgroup/3` -> {"batch_size_dynamic_cap":64} — started rollout to 6 nodes.

alex_oncall: Good. Also bump `kv_cache_retention_ms` up a bit to reduce evictions caused by long KVs? Jia, can you estimate safe value?

jia_runtime: Increasing kv retention from 60s -> 180s should reduce thrash. I'll stage on a small canary set.

nina_support: Message for CS: "We're investigating higher latencies affecting a subset of customers in US-W2. We're applying temporary mitigations and will update in 30m." Want me to post now?

alex_oncall: Yes, please post a short status update. Include that requests are progressing and that a mitigation is being rolled out.

[~8m later]

sam_sre: Rollout completed to initial 6 nodes, metrics show p95 falling to ~210ms, p99 trending down to 950ms. Streaming stalls reduced but still visible for some sessions.

jia_runtime: Can confirm kv eviction rate dropped ~4x after retention bump on canary nodes. Padding amplification also reduced (p95 batch size down to 24).

alex_oncall: Next steps: 1) continue rollout to remainder of pool; 2) schedule short_seq prioritization to be enabled after full rollout; 3) run incident-postmortem checklist. If rollout reverts, we'll flip to model-variant fallback.

deploy-bot: Rollout to remaining nodes started. Progress updates: 20% -> 50% -> 80% -> 100%.

nina_support: Posted status to affected tenants and CS.

sam_sre: Metrics now stable for 5m: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms. Streaming stall rate down by ~70%. Logging final mitigation parameters: `batch_size_dynamic_cap=64`, `kv_cache_retention_ms=180`, `favor_short_seq=true` (staged).

alex_oncall: Handing off to night oncall at 1777777800. Key context for handoff: root cause likely padding amplification from mixed sequence lengths exacerbated by scheduler fairness issues; mitigations applied (batch cap + kv retention). If p99 rises above 1.5s or streaming stall rate >5% revert to safe-mode: `batching_mode=latency-first` and open page to eng-sre.

jia_runtime: I'll prepare a reproducer and a follow-up task: add adaptive batch caps per-request-hint (streaming vs non-streaming) and better short-request prioritization.

alex_oncall: Thanks team. Filing incident ticket and postmortem. Leaving channel open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
